label: Fresh vegetables venture
text: Need: people want fresh vegetables but shelf life is short. Evaluation: people are ready to pay more; maintenance cost. Exploitation: processed vegetables with technology, packed and hygienic food on the shop, higher price, profit, minimization of loss.

label: Davidsson (2005)
text: Entrepreneurship makes a difference, or else it isn't entrepreneurship.

label: Wickham (2006) diagram
text: Small business sits in a small corner; the entrepreneurial venture extends far further on growth potential, innovation and strategic objectives.

label: Growing versus scaling
text: Growing: costs rise almost as fast as revenues. Scaling: revenues rise steeply while costs rise slowly.

label: Bhave (1994) process of emergence
text: An iterative, nonlinear, feedback driven, conceptual and physical process, drawn as a tangled line that straightens from research to concept prototype to design.

label: Emerged vs non-emergent ventures
text: Emerged: high rate, low concentration, late timing of activities. Non-emergent: low rate, high concentration, early timing.

label: Grace Orchard School, Singapore
text: Two churches collaborated to start a government-aided private school for children with special educational needs. The government funds the location and the recurrent cost; the alliance partners provide the management, recruit volunteers and consider long-term financial support. Example of a community-based enterprise.

label: Banyan Tree Gallery (BTG)
text: An extension of the social consciousness of Banyan Tree Holiday Resorts (BTHR), which built environmentally sensitive luxury boutique resorts steeped in Asian traditions. The Phuket resort was a disused 400-hectare tin mining site called 'too severely ravaged' to sustain development in a 1977 United Nations report; the team preserved the remaining trees, planted 800 new ones and created six lagoons stocked with fish, tiger prawns, shrimp and other animals. BTG was founded in 1994 when triangular cushions made by female Thai villagers were incorporated into Banyan Tree Phuket. Example of a socially responsible enterprise.

label: Northern Leaf Communications (NLC)
text: A PR firm specializing in Internet design, corporate design, marketing communications and launching events. After its first successful collaboration with the Children's Cancer Foundation in 1995 (raising funds and awareness), it used the charity angle to approach companies and pitched for more non-profit projects; its main clients are now about twenty non-profit organizations. It couples its business objective with its clients' social goals. Example of social service industry professionals.

label: Transnational Recycling Industries Pte Ltd
text: Specializes in paper materials, old newspapers & corrugated, computer & waste paper. It gathers recyclable materials from households and sells them to a recycling company, using part of its profits for community projects. The materials cost nothing and only collection costs are incurred, so it benefits greatly if the quantity collected increases. Example of a socio-economic or dualistic enterprise.

label: Impact investing market size
text: The global impact investing market will be at least $500 billion within the next decade, yet most hybrid entrepreneurs still experience difficulty in raising capital.

label: Barro's Microsoft Windows example
text: Harvard University economist Robert Barro argued Microsoft has been a boon for society and the market value of its software greatly exceeds the likely value of Mr. Gates' philanthropic efforts. If a copy of Windows sells for $50, revenue is $50 times the copies sold; earnings are revenue less production and development expenses; social value comes from the increase in productivity when businesses and households use the software, and equals the value of the extra product less the total paid for the software.
